---
title: "Measurement"
subtitle: "What is measured, what is not, and why a figure that exists can still not be a result."
---

## The short version

The harness decides what may be published, and right now it is saying "not this". Every eval
report in the repository is marked `quotable_as_a_result: false` with its reason, and the build
refuses to publish a figure from any of them.

That gate is the point of this page. A benchmark that only reports when the answer is flattering
is not a benchmark, so this one reports the reason instead of the number.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  R[("reports/eval/<br/><small>8 reports</small>")] --> Q{"quotable_as<br/>_a_result?"}
  Q -->|"false, all 8"| S["Stated absence<br/><small>with the report's own reason</small>"]
  Q -->|"true"| N["Published number<br/><small>with its interval</small>"]
  S --> P["Page"]
  N --> P
  style N stroke-dasharray: 4 3
```

The dashed path has not been taken yet: `{{< var unmeasured_metrics >}}` of
`{{< var total_metrics >}}` headline metrics are still waiting on the two inputs below. The left
path is what the pages show today, and it carries the reason rather than a blank.

## Why a figure can exist and not be a result

Three distinct reasons, and the difference between them is the whole point.

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Synthetic fixtures

A bundle generated from a spec rather than recorded from a running system.

**The single largest finding in this project** is that fixtures are a *different scale of
difficulty*, not merely an easier one. The same deterministic triage:

| Data | Root cause named correctly |
|---|---|
| Synthetic fixtures | almost all of them |
| Real recordings | {{< var recorded_root_cause_correct >}} of {{< var recorded_root_cause_applicable >}} |

The threshold tuned on fixtures found a gap so wide it was implausible: the loudest quiet
system scored 7.7 and the quietest real incident 66.8, with no overlap at all. On recordings
those populations overlap badly. A tuning run on fixtures produced a number that looked
excellent and generalised poorly, which is the outcome this project exists to make visible
rather than to avoid.

### A partly recorded split

Eight of sixteen validation scenarios are recorded. A figure over those eight is a *real
measurement of a small sample*: true about the eight, silent about the split.

Reported with a bootstrap confidence interval rather than as a bare number, because an accuracy
over eight incidents and one over eighty are not the same kind of statement.

### A tuning split

Thresholds and prompts were chosen using `validation`. A figure from it measures **fit**, not
performance.

Only `test_id` and `test_ood` can ever support a claim about performance, and test results are
computed once per release candidate. Both are currently empty.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## And a report can go stale, which is worse than a missing one

One report in this repository was computed over a single recorded incident that was later
deleted for recording corruption. It describes a state that no longer exists, while still
satisfying "every number traces to a report".

So the build checks a report's recorded count against the bundles present and refuses to
publish from one that no longer matches. "Traceable" was not a strong enough property on its
own.
:::

## Two test splits, not one

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  LIB["{{< var specs >}} scenario specs"] --> TRAIN["train<br/><small>39, development</small>"]
  LIB --> VAL["validation<br/><small>16, tuning</small>"]
  LIB --> TID["test_id<br/><small>29, held out</small>"]
  LIB --> TOOD["test_ood<br/><small>30, whole families held out</small>"]
  TRAIN --> TUNE["Thresholds, prompts, memory"]
  VAL --> TUNE
  TID --> CLAIM["The only figures that<br/>may be called a result"]
  TOOD --> CLAIM
  style TUNE fill:#fff8e8,stroke:#e6cf9a
```

They answer different questions:

- **In-distribution** holds back variants, loads and seeds of fault types seen in development.
  It asks *does it work*.
- **Out-of-distribution** holds back **whole fault families**. It asks *did it generalise or
  memorise*.

Splitting is by scenario spec, not by recording, so a second recording of the same fault cannot
leak an answer across the boundary.

## Seven graders, and the one that exists to prevent a lie

| Grader | Asks |
|---|---|
| `root_cause` | Is the named service the injected one, at rank 1 |
| `root_cause_top3` | Is it anywhere in the top three |
| `abstention` | Did it abstain exactly when it should have |
| `fault_class` | Is the mechanism right, not just the service |
| `onset` | How far off is the stated start time |
| `evidence_validity` | Does every citation re-run to the same bytes |
| `remediation` | Would the proposal have fixed it |

The pair that matters is the first and the third. A single grader scoring both identification
and abstention would let **a system that abstains on everything look like one that identifies
everything**. So a no-fault incident is *not applicable* to the root-cause grader, and that is
reported rather than counted as a pass.

## How a comparison is decided

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["Candidate"] --> P["Paired by incident"]
  B["Baseline"] --> P
  P --> BOOT["Paired bootstrap"]
  BOOT --> I{"Does the interval<br/>exclude zero?"}
  I -->|"no"| X["Not a difference.<br/>Nothing ships"]
  I -->|"yes"| Y["A measured difference"]
```

Paired by incident, not two independent samples, so the interval reflects the same incidents
being compared. A difference whose interval includes zero **is not a difference**, and nothing
ships on one.

The gate that enforces this reports `INCONCLUSIVE` separately from `FAIL`, because "a
regression was measured" and "the split is too small to rule one out" need different responses:
the first is a bug, the second is a recording session.

## Baselines

| Configuration | Is |
|---|---|
| `b0` | Deterministic triage alone, no model. **The floor any agent must beat** |
| `b1` | A single-agent ReAct loop with the same tools |
| `b2` | The same loop without the knowledge graph |
| `fb-v1` | The full system |
| `a1` to `a6` | Ablations, each removing one component |

`b0` is the important one. A multi-agent system that cannot beat a page of statistics should not
exist, and the comparison is reported whichever way it comes out.

## Engineering, as distinct from performance

These are facts about the repository, not results about the system.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tests | {{< var tests_passed >}} passing, {{< var tests_skipped >}} skipped |
| Coverage | {{< var coverage_percent >}}%, against an exact 85% floor |
| Decision records | {{< var adrs >}} |

::: {.callout-note}
A passing test says the code does what a test says it should. It says nothing about whether
Firebreak finds root causes. Keeping those two ideas apart is most of what this page is for.
:::
